blocks.en: Planning Evangelistic Sermons – Textual and Expository Approaches
blocks.es_reference: Planificación de Sermones Evangelísticos – Los Enfoques Textual y Expositivo
Idioma:
Vía:
Objetivo de Aprendizaje

blocks.en: After studying this unit you will be able to use the Textual and Expository Approaches taught in WiseSpeak to plan a complete evangelistic sermon.
blocks.es_reference: Después de estudiar esta unidad podrá usar los Enfoques Textual y Expositivo enseñados en WiseSpeak para planificar un sermón evangelístico completo.

blocks.en: The Textual and Expository Approaches in WiseSpeak
blocks.es_reference: Los Enfoques Textual y Expositivo en WiseSpeak

blocks.en: WiseSpeak teaches two closely related planning methods that keep the sermon anchored in a single passage of Scripture. The Textual Approach takes one clear verse or short paragraph and lets its specific facts shape the entire sermon. The Expository Approach moves verse by verse through a longer passage, drawing out the main truths as it goes. These approaches are powerful for evangelistic preaching because they let the Bible speak for itself. The listener sees that the message comes directly from God's Word.
blocks.es_reference: WiseSpeak enseña dos métodos de planificación estrechamente relacionados que mantienen el sermón anclado en un solo pasaje de las Escrituras. El Enfoque Textual toma un versículo claro o un párrafo corto y deja que sus hechos específicos formen todo el sermón. El Enfoque Expositivo avanza versículo por versículo a través de un pasaje más largo, extrayendo las verdades principales a medida que avanza. Estos enfoques son poderosos para la predicación evangelística porque dejan que la Biblia hable por sí misma. El oyente ve que el mensaje proviene directamente de la Palabra de Dios.
El Enfoque Inductivo

blocks.en: Both methods follow the inductive approach from the first seven units of WiseSpeak. We begin with the specific facts in the text and work backward to discover the keyword and subject.
blocks.es_reference: Ambos métodos siguen el enfoque inductivo de las primeras siete unidades de WiseSpeak. Comenzamos con los hechos específicos del texto y trabajamos hacia atrás para descubrir la palabra clave y el tema.
Cómo Funciona el Enfoque Textual

blocks.en: Choose one clear verse or short paragraph.
blocks.es_reference: Elegir un versículo claro o un párrafo corto.

blocks.en: Read it carefully and ask the probing question the text answers.
blocks.es_reference: Leerlo con cuidado y hacer la pregunta de sondeo que el texto responde.

blocks.en: Identify the key idea and turn it into a plural noun keyword.
blocks.es_reference: Identificar la idea clave y convertirla en una palabra clave (sustantivo plural).

blocks.en: Form the subject around the keyword.
blocks.es_reference: Formar el tema alrededor de la palabra clave.

blocks.en: List the specific facts or truths in the text. Turn each truth into a short point (five words or less) that is a singular of the keyword.
blocks.es_reference: Listar los hechos o verdades específicos del texto. Convertir cada verdad en un punto corto (cinco palabras o menos) que sea un singular de la palabra clave.
Escribir un objetivo evangelístico de una sola oración.

blocks.en: Add a clear invitation at the end.
blocks.es_reference: Agregar una invitación clara al final.
Ejemplo Textual — Juan 3:16

blocks.en: The text answers the question, "Why did God send His Son?" The keyword is "reasons" (a plural noun). The subject is "Three Reasons God Sent His Son."
blocks.es_reference: El texto responde a la pregunta: "¿Por qué envió Dios a Su Hijo?" La palabra clave es "razones" (un sustantivo plural). El tema es "Tres Razones por las que Dios Envió a Su Hijo".

blocks.en: Question: Why did God send His Son? · Keyword: reasons
blocks.es_reference: Pregunta: ¿Por qué envió Dios a Su Hijo? · Palabra clave: razones
Razón Uno: Mostrar Su amor.
Razón Dos: Ofrecer vida eterna.
Razón Tres: Salvar al mundo.
Ejemplo Textual — Romanos 10:9

blocks.en: The text answers the question, "How can I be saved?" The keyword is "conditions" (a plural noun). The subject is "God's Conditions for Salvation."
blocks.es_reference: El texto responde a la pregunta: "¿Cómo puedo ser salvo?" La palabra clave es "condiciones" (un sustantivo plural). El tema es "Las Condiciones de Dios para la Salvación".

blocks.en: Question: How can I be saved? · Keyword: conditions
blocks.es_reference: Pregunta: ¿Cómo puedo ser salvo? · Palabra clave: condiciones
Condición Uno: Confesar con la boca.
Condición Dos: Creer en el corazón.
Condición Tres: Recibir la salvación de Dios.
Cómo Funciona el Enfoque Expositivo

blocks.en: The Expository Approach moves through a longer passage verse by verse. We still use the same keyword rules. We read the entire passage, discover the central idea, select the plural noun keyword, form the subject, and then draw three short parallel points from the key truths in the passage.
blocks.es_reference: El Enfoque Expositivo avanza a través de un pasaje más largo versículo por versículo. Todavía usamos las mismas reglas de la palabra clave. Leemos todo el pasaje, descubrimos la idea central, seleccionamos la palabra clave (sustantivo plural), formamos el tema y luego extraemos tres puntos cortos y paralelos de las verdades clave del pasaje.
Ejemplo Expositivo — Lucas 15:11–32

blocks.en: The passage answers the question, "Can God still accept me after what I have done?" The keyword is "reasons" (a plural noun). The subject is "Three Reasons God Welcomes You Home."
blocks.es_reference: El pasaje responde a la pregunta: "¿Puede Dios todavía aceptarme después de lo que he hecho?" La palabra clave es "razones" (un sustantivo plural). El tema es "Tres Razones por las que Dios Te Recibe en Casa".

blocks.en: Question: Can God still accept me after what I have done? · Keyword: reasons
blocks.es_reference: Pregunta: ¿Puede Dios todavía aceptarme después de lo que he hecho? · Palabra clave: razones
Razón Uno: Amor del Padre.
Razón Dos: Brazos abiertos.
Razón Tres: Restauración completa.

blocks.en: The sermon moves through the story of the prodigal son but stays unified under one clear keyword.
blocks.es_reference: El sermón avanza a través de la historia del hijo pródigo pero se mantiene unificado bajo una sola palabra clave clara.

blocks.en: Why These Approaches Are Powerful for Evangelistic Preaching
blocks.es_reference: Por Qué Estos Enfoques Son Poderosos para la Predicación Evangelística

blocks.en: The Textual and Expository Approaches keep every sermon biblical. The listener knows the points come straight from Scripture. The plural noun keyword gives the whole sermon unity. These methods work especially well when the text itself raises a question people today are still asking. When a single verse does not contain every point needed, we add supporting texts from other passages while the keyword still controls the outline.
blocks.es_reference: Los Enfoques Textual y Expositivo mantienen cada sermón bíblico. El oyente sabe que los puntos provienen directamente de las Escrituras. La palabra clave (sustantivo plural) da unidad a todo el sermón. Estos métodos funcionan especialmente bien cuando el texto mismo plantea una pregunta que la gente hoy todavía se hace. Cuando un solo versículo no contiene cada punto necesario, simplemente agregamos textos de apoyo de otros pasajes mientras la palabra clave controla el bosquejo.

blocks.en: Practical Steps to Use the Textual and Expository Approaches in Your Preaching
blocks.es_reference: Pasos Prácticos para Usar los Enfoques Textual y Expositivo en Su Predicación

blocks.en: Choose a clear text or short passage, read it carefully, and write the probing question it answers; then follow the steps above. These approaches, taught in WiseSpeak, turn any biblical text into a powerful evangelistic sermon that is clear, memorable, and aimed at the heart.
blocks.es_reference: Elegir un texto claro o un pasaje corto, leerlo con cuidado y escribir la pregunta de sondeo que responde; luego seguir los pasos de arriba. Estos enfoques, enseñados en WiseSpeak, convierten cualquier texto bíblico en un sermón evangelístico poderoso que es claro, memorable y apuntado al corazón.

mc.stem: What sermon-planning approaches does this unit teach?
options: Word Method and Question Method
Allegorical Method and Topical Method
Interview Method and Word Method
Textual Approach and Expository Approach

mc.stem: The Textual Approach takes:
options: Several unrelated verses from different books
A whole chapter of narrative material
One clear verse or short paragraph and lets its specific facts shape the entire sermon
The preacher's personal life experience

mc.stem: The Expository Approach:
options: Begins with a topic and gathers proof-texts from across Scripture
Moves verse by verse through a longer passage, drawing out main truths as it goes
Builds the sermon around the preacher's interview with a known person
Allegorizes the text to find hidden symbolic meanings

mc.stem: Both the Textual and Expository Approaches follow which method?
options: Inductive — begin with the text's specific facts and work backward
Allegorical — symbolic meaning behind the words
Deductive — topic first, then proof-texts
Anecdotal — begin with a personal story

mc.stem: In the John 3:16 (Textual) example, the question the text answers is:
options: How can I be saved?
Why did God send His Son?
Can God still accept me after what I have done?
What must I do to inherit eternal life?

mc.stem: In the John 3:16 example, the keyword chosen is:
options: reasons
sources
conditions
proofs

mc.stem: In the John 3:16 example, the three points are:
options: Hear gospel; Believe in Jesus; Be baptized
Confess with mouth; Believe in heart; Receive salvation
Father's love; Open arms; Full restoration
Show His love; Offer eternal life; Save the world

mc.stem: In the Romans 10:9 (Textual) example, the question the text answers is:
options: Why did God send His Son?
Can God still accept me?
How can I be saved?
Where does eternal life begin?

mc.stem: In the Romans 10:9 example, the keyword chosen is:
options: conditions
reasons
steps
proofs

mc.stem: In the Romans 10:9 example, the three points are:
options: Show His love; Offer eternal life; Save the world
Confess with your mouth; Believe in your heart; Receive God's salvation
Christ died for us; While we were sinners; God demonstrates love
Father's love; Open arms; Full restoration

mc.stem: In the Luke 15:11–32 (Expository) example, the question the passage answers is:
options: How can I find real satisfaction?
Why did God send His Son?
Can God still accept me after what I have done?
What must I do to be saved?

mc.stem: In the Luke 15:11–32 example, the keyword chosen is:
options: conditions
steps
proofs
reasons

mc.stem: In the Luke 15:11–32 example, the three points are:
options: Father's love; Open arms; Full restoration
Show His love; Offer eternal life; Save the world
Living water; True worship; Personal testimony
Hear the gospel; Believe in Jesus; Be baptized

mc.stem: The keyword in both the Textual and Expository Approaches must be:
options: A verb in the imperative mood
An adjective describing the listener
A proper name from the passage
A plural noun drawn from the text

mc.stem: The maximum length of each outline point is:
options: Ten words or less
Five words or less
Twelve words or less
A complete sentence of any length

mc.stem: The chief difference between the Textual Approach and the Expository Approach is:
options: One uses the New Testament; the other uses only the Old
One is preached in the morning; the other in the evening
The Textual focuses on one verse or short paragraph; the Expository moves through a longer passage verse by verse
The Textual requires three points; the Expository requires seven

mc.stem: When a single verse does not contain every point needed:
options: The preacher must abandon the keyword discipline
Supporting texts are added from other passages while the keyword still controls the outline
The sermon must be reduced to one point only
The Textual Approach is replaced by an allegorical one

mc.stem: What is the FIRST step in the Textual Approach?
options: Add a clear invitation at the end
Write the one-sentence evangelistic objective
Choose one clear verse or short paragraph
Form the subject around the keyword

mc.stem: The three biblical texts used as worked examples in this unit are:
options: John 3:16, Romans 10:9, and Luke 15:11–32
John 4, Romans 5:8, and Acts 16
Genesis 1, Exodus 20, and Psalm 23
Acts 2:38, John 1:1, and Matthew 28:19

mc.stem: Why are the Textual and Expository Approaches especially powerful for evangelistic preaching?
options: They make the sermon shorter and easier to preach without preparation
They allow the preacher to avoid mentioning sin or judgment
They reduce the role of the keyword to optional decoration
They let the Bible speak for itself so the listener sees the message comes directly from God's Word

sa.prompt: Define both the Textual Approach and the Expository Approach in your own words.
sa.model: The Textual Approach takes one clear verse or short paragraph and lets its specific facts shape the whole sermon. The Expository Approach moves verse by verse through a longer passage, drawing out its truths. Both are inductive and built on a plural-noun keyword.

sa.prompt: List the seven steps for using the Textual Approach.
sa.model: The seven steps are: choose the verse, read it carefully, ask the probing question, select the plural-noun keyword, form the subject, build the short parallel points and objective, and close with the invitation.

sa.prompt: In the John 3:16 example, what is the question, what is the keyword, and what are the three points?
sa.model: In the John 3:16 example the question is 'Why did God send His Son?' The keyword is 'reasons,' and the three points are: show His love, offer eternal life, save the world.

sa.prompt: In the Romans 10:9 example, what is the question, what is the keyword, and what are the three points?
sa.model: In the Romans 10:9 example the question is 'How can I be saved?' The keyword is 'conditions,' and the three points are: confess with your mouth, believe in your heart, receive God's salvation.

sa.prompt: In the Luke 15 (Expository) example, what is the question, what is the keyword, and what are the three points?
sa.model: In the Luke 15 expository example the question is 'Can God still accept me?' The keyword is 'reasons,' and the three points are: the Father's love, His open arms, full restoration - showing why God welcomes the returning sinner.

sa.prompt: How does the Textual Approach differ from the Expository Approach in scope of the text used?
sa.model: The two differ in scope: the Textual Approach uses one verse or short paragraph and lets its facts shape the sermon, while the Expository Approach works through a longer passage verse by verse, drawing the outline from the unfolding text.

sa.prompt: Why does this unit say the Textual and Expository Approaches are especially powerful for evangelistic preaching?
sa.model: These approaches are especially powerful for evangelism because they let the Bible speak for itself: the listener sees the message comes directly from God's Word, which gives it biblical authority while the keyword keeps it unified and memorable.

sa.prompt: State the keyword rule and the points rule that govern both approaches.
sa.model: Both approaches are governed by the same two rules: the keyword must be a plural noun, and every point must be a short, parallel singular of that keyword, five words or less.

sa.prompt: How do these approaches handle the case when a single verse does not contain every point needed?
sa.model: When one verse does not contain every point, these approaches add supporting texts, but the keyword still controls the outline so the added passages stay unified under one plural-noun keyword.

sa.prompt: According to this unit, what do the Textual and Expository Approaches turn a biblical text into for the listener, and why is that effective in evangelism?
sa.model: These approaches turn a biblical text into a clear, memorable sermon that the listener sees comes straight from Scripture. That is effective in evangelism because the message carries God's own authority and presses the text directly on the heart toward a decision.
